name: LaTeX
summary: Document markup language and macro package built on TeX: authors describe logical structure (sections, environments, cross-references, floats) and document classes and packages turn it into typeset output. The current kernel is LaTeX2e (since 1994), maintained by the LaTeX Project, with the expl3 programming layer (LaTeX3) now loaded in the format.

level_notes.0: The definition is the kernel source itself: latex3/latex2e (base/*.dtx literate sources, built into latex.ltx) plus the expl3 kernel in latex3/latex3, run on a TeX engine (pdfTeX, XeTeX, LuaTeX; see the tex entry). The l3build regression suite (base/testfiles) is the de-facto conformance test. LaTeXML, plasTeX, LaTeX.js, Pandoc, KaTeX/MathJax and Tectonic are alternative (often partial) implementations or converters.
level_notes.1: There is no formal standard. Authoritative are Lamport's book (LaTeX: A Document Preparation System, paywalled), the LaTeX Project's guides (usrguide, clsguide, fntguide, lthooks-doc, interface3) and the documented sources (source2e). The LaTeX2e unofficial reference manual (latexref.xyz) is the most complete open reference and is used here for section-level deep links.
level_notes.2: learnlatex.org (by LaTeX Project members), the Wikibooks LaTeX book and Overleaf Learn are the main open tutorials; TUGboat/LaTeX Project papers cover design and history.
level_notes.3: Wikipedia, PLDB, CTAN and the TeX FAQ index the ecosystem.
